6º de Primaria · Inglés

Describing people and places

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

«What does she look like?» y «What is she like?» parecen casi iguales. ¿Preguntan lo mismo?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

No. What does she look like? pregunta por su aspecto: «She's tall and she has got long hair». What is she like? pregunta por su forma de ser: «She's kind and funny». Con las dos podemos hacer una descripción completa.

2

Aprende9 bloques cortos

Appearance: body and face

To describe appearance (aspecto) we use be and have got. With be: «He is tall / short / medium height», «She is young / old», «They are slim / strong».

With have got: «She has got blue eyes», «He has got a beard / a moustache / freckles (pecas)». We also say «He wears glasses». En castellano: en inglés no se dice «es de ojos azules», sino «tiene ojos azules»: has got blue eyes. Y los adjetivos no tienen plural: «blue eyes», nunca «blues eyes».

Hair

For hair we usually say length, then style, then colour: long / short / medium-length, straight / wavy / curly, blond / brown / black / red / grey. «She's got long curly brown hair», «He's got short straight black hair». We can also say «He's bald» (calvo) or «She has got a ponytail» (coleta).

En castellano: hair es incontable cuando hablamos del pelo de la cabeza: «Her hair is long», no «her hairs are».

Personality

To describe personality (carácter) we ask What is he like?. Positive adjectives: kind (amable), friendly (simpático), funny (gracioso), clever (listo), brave (valiente), hard-working (trabajador), generous, patient, calm.

Negative ones: lazy (vago), bossy (mandón), shy (tímido, not really negative!), rude (maleducado), moody. Give an example to show it: «My grandpa is very patient: he always helps me with my homework». Consejo: usa very, quite y a bit para matizar.

Adjective order

In English, adjectives go before the noun: «a big house», never «a house big». When there are several, they follow an order: opinion – size – age – shape – colour – material + noun.

«a beautiful old castle», «a small round wooden table», «a nice big red bike». En castellano: en español el adjetivo suele ir detrás («una casa grande»), por eso en inglés hay que pensar al revés. No uses más de dos o tres adjetivos seguidos.

Describing places

To describe a place we use there is / there are and adjectives: «My town is small and quiet. There is a beautiful beach and there are some old churches. There isn't a cinema».

Useful adjectives for places: big, small, busy (con mucha gente), quiet (tranquilo), noisy (ruidoso), modern, old, clean, dirty, crowded, peaceful. En castellano: empieza por lo general (cómo es) y luego explica qué hay.

Where is it? Prepositions of place

Prepositions of place say where things are: in (dentro), on (encima), under (debajo), next to (al lado de), between (entre), behind (detrás), in front of (delante de), opposite (enfrente de), near (cerca).

«The lamp is next to the bed», «The cat is under the desk», «The bank is opposite the park», «The school is between the library and the pool». En castellano: ojo con in front of (delante) y opposite (enfrente, al otro lado).

Vídeo: In front of, behind, between: prepositions song · Maple Leaf Learning (YouTube) · 5,8 millones de visualizaciones

Reading: my best friend and my street

Read Adam's description: «My best friend is Sofía. She's quite tall and she has got short wavy black hair and big brown eyes. She wears glasses. She's very funny and kind, but a bit shy with new people. She lives in my street. It's a quiet street with tall trees. There's a bakery next to her house and there's a small park opposite my flat. We play there every afternoon».

Writing a description

Plan your description in three paragraphs (párrafos): 1) Who and appearance («My uncle Javi is tall…»), 2) personality with examples («He's very generous: he always…»), 3) place or activities («He lives in a flat near the sea…»).

Use connectors: and, but, also, because. «She's shy but very friendly», «I like him because he's funny». Consejo: relee tu texto para comprobar el orden de los adjetivos y que hayas usado has got con los ojos y el pelo.

Let's practise: Guess who?

Play «Guess who?» with pictures of people or classmates (with respect!). Ask only yes/no questions: «Has he got curly hair?» – «No, he hasn't». «Is she wearing a red jumper?» – «Yes, she is». «Does he wear glasses?» – «Yes, he does».

Then describe a place in the classroom without saying its name: «It's next to the window and opposite the door. There are lots of books on it». Your partner guesses: «The bookshelf!». Consejo: describe con respeto, sin palabras que puedan molestar a nadie.

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Order the words: «hair / she / got / long / blond / has».

  1. Sujeto + has got.
  2. Longitud antes que color: long blond hair.

Resultado: She has got long blond hair.

Ejemplo 2. Answer «What is your best friend like?» with two adjectives.

  1. Pregunta por el carácter, no por el aspecto.
  2. Dos adjetivos y un ejemplo.

Resultado: He's funny and generous: he always shares his snacks.

Ejemplo 3. Describe where the cat is: (debajo de la mesa, al lado de la puerta)

  1. debajo = under.
  2. al lado de = next to.

Resultado: The cat is under the table, next to the door.

Errores típicos

  • Poner el adjetivo detrás: «a house big» → «a big house».
  • Poner plural al adjetivo: «blues eyes» → «blue eyes».
  • Decir «hairs» para el pelo de la cabeza → «hair».
  • Confundir What is he like? (carácter) con What does he look like? (aspecto).
  • Usar is en lugar de has got: «She is blue eyes» → «She has got blue eyes».

Ejercicios

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

  1. Translate: «Tiene el pelo corto y rizado.»

    Ver solución
    She has got short curly hair (o He has got…).

  2. Order: «car / red / a / small».

    Ver solución
    a small red car.

  3. Write the opposite: tall, quiet, lazy, old.

    Ver solución
    short, noisy, hard-working, young (o new).

  4. Which question asks about personality?

    Ver solución
    What is he like?

  5. Complete: «The bank is ___ the park.» (enfrente de)

    Ver solución
    opposite.

  6. Complete: «My bag is ___ my chair.» (debajo de)

    Ver solución
    under.

  7. Correct: «My sister has got browns eyes.»

    Ver solución
    My sister has got brown eyes.

  8. Complete: «There ___ two parks in my town.»

    Ver solución
    are.

  9. Describe your bedroom in two sentences.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: There is a bed next to the window. My desk is opposite the door.

  10. Describe a family member in three sentences.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: My mum is tall. She has got short brown hair. She's very kind and funny.

Para familias

  • Jugad en casa a «Guess who?» con fotos de la familia, preguntando en inglés.
  • Describid juntos vuestra calle en inglés con tres frases con there is / there are.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.
